title: Circle's Arc L1 - the issuer-run, permissioned 'Wall Street blockchain' (credibility: not decentralized)
source: Public record: Circle (NYSE: CRCL) Arc announcements (introduced 12 Aug 2025; testnet 28 Oct 2025; founding validators 5 Aug 2026; mainnet 16 Sep 2026); crypto-press coverage. Overlay on the stablecoin-L1 landscape (peer to Tempo). HONESTY: architecture, validator set, dates = fact (corroborated across independent outlets); presale/valuation/benchmark figures = reported (not from Circle filings, treat as reported/varies); the credibility read (permissioned-PoA, issuer-run-conflict, 'public blockchain' branding) = clearly-labeled interpretation.

edges.notes: Jeremy Allaire co-founded + runs Circle (USDC issuer; NYSE: CRCL) - which built Arc; Circle's Q2-2026 revenue was ~95% reserve income, so Arc is its pivot from single-product issuer to fee-capturing infrastructure operator (fact; strategic-pivot framing lightly interpretive).

Circle built + controls Arc - an EVM (Reth) L1 with Malachite (Tendermint-BFT, Informal Systems) deterministic finality <500ms, ~3,000 TPS at 20 validators; introduced 12 Aug 2025, testnet 28 Oct 2025, mainnet 16 Sep 2026. CREDIBILITY: the ISSUER runs the chain - vertical integration (issue USDC + operate the settlement layer + capture fees), like Tether/Cantor + Stripe/Tempo (fact of structure; conflict framing interpretation).

USDC is Arc's native gas token (fees ~$0.01, EIP-1559 smoothed) - the issuer's own stablecoin is the fee currency; deterministic finality removes reorg risk (a real institutional-settlement advantage) (fact).

Arc is a stablecoin-native settlement L1 for institutional finance; it processed 700M+ testnet tx across 2.8M wallets pre-launch (reported figures) and launched ONE DAY after the 15 Sep 2026 CLARITY cloture failure - a compliance-first bet on eventual US clarity (fact of timing).

Arc (Circle) vs Tempo (Stripe/Paradigm) are the two flagship stablecoin-payment L1s - the ISSUER-run chain vs the PROCESSOR-run chain; the emerging L1 race to own stablecoin settlement (fact of category; also Tether's Plasma/Stable, Ripple, Codex in the wider field).

Arc's permissioned, compliance-first design is a bet that regulation (CLARITY/GENIUS) will favor institutional, KYC-gated rails; mainnet timing (day after the failed cloture vote) underscores the dependence on that clarity (fact of timing; interpretation of the bet).

BlackRock is one of 11 permissioned institutional validators AND a presale backer AND plans to migrate its ~$2.87B BUIDL tokenized-Treasury fund onto Arc - deepening the BlackRock<->Circle<->Treasuries loop (fact; migration is announced/forward-looking).

DTCC (the US securities clearing backbone) is a validator and plans to begin tokenizing DTC-custodied assets on Arc in 2027 - a core market-plumbing institution on an issuer-run chain (fact of announcement; 2027 forward-looking).
Visa is among the 11 founding validators - a card network helping run a stablecoin settlement L1 while also pursuing its own USDC settlement (fact).
Mastercard is a founding Arc validator (while also partnering Circle + owning BVNK) - incumbent networks hedging into stablecoin rails (fact).
Standard Chartered is a founding validator - a global bank on the permissioned set (fact).
SBI Group (Japan) is a founding validator - Asian financial-group participation (fact).

Galaxy Digital is a founding validator; the full 11 also include Global Payments, ICE (NYSE parent), MoneyGram, and Sumitomo - reportedly the most concentrated institutional validator set ever assembled for a public-blockchain launch (fact of set; 'most concentrated' = reported). CREDIBILITY: this is proof-of-AUTHORITY - Circle-chosen permissioned validators, NOT permissionless; a feature for TradFi trust + a censorship/control risk (interpretation).

a16z crypto led the ARC token presale (reported ~$222M at ~$3B valuation), with BlackRock + Apollo among backers; Circle minted 10B ARC as a technical milestone but has NOT committed to a public token launch - token status is uncertain/speculative (fact of presale reports; figures reported/varies).
Apollo (private-credit/asset-management giant) is among the reported ARC presale backers - TradFi private capital into the issuer's chain (fact of reported backing).
